sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5026 .H64 1989
sources.note: Sec. 4.2.1 Mari, printed p. 51: Table 4.1 phonemes (p b mp mb m; t nt nd n s z r; k ngk ngg ng g h; w y; i a u) + 3 segmental notes (/g/ allophony, /r/ [r]~[l]~[d], prenasalised stops rare). Nothing on stress, accent, tone, syllables or prosody. Ch. 4 intro p. 50: 'Full phonological statements are to be published at a later date' (none appeared). The book's only 'stress' hits concern Adzera dialect perception, Duwet unstressed vowel sequences and a Watut historical remark.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1986. A morphology and grammar of Adzera (Amari dialect), Morobe Province, PNG. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 24, PL A-70, 77-166
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.5 Stress p. 94: 'Stress in Amari is not phonemic. In general, the first syllable of a two-syllable word is stressed, and in words of more than two syllables, the first syllable is stressed, and then every alternate syllable'. This is ADZERA (adze1240), the Mari people's neighbour/second language, not Mari; contains no statement about Mari and is not used as one.

sources.note: The only primary recordings of Mari; an instrumental/auditory check of stress placement would have to start from these, since no written statement exists.
